---
title: "Installation & getting started"
---

This page walks you through installing the dependencies and running your first training example.

## 1. Install pixi

AIHydroPoints uses [pixi](https://pixi.sh) to manage Julia and all other dependencies.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Linux / macOS

```bash
curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh
```

Restart your shell (or `source ~/.bashrc`) so that `pixi` is on your PATH.

### Windows

```powershell
winget install prefix-dev.pixi
```

Or with PowerShell:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm -useb https://pixi.sh/install.ps1 | iex"
```

:::

## 2. Clone the repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Deltares-research/AIHydroPoints.jl.git
cd AIHydroPoints.jl
```

::: {.callout-tip}
If `git` is not available on your system, you can install it via pixi:
```bash
pixi global install git
```
:::


## 3. Install the environment

```bash
pixi install
```

This downloads Julia (via juliaup) and all conda dependencies declared in `pixi.toml`.

## 4. Install Julia

```bash
pixi run install-julia
```

This installs the pinned Julia version (1.12.5) through juliaup.

## 5. Instantiate the Julia project

```bash
pixi run julia --project -e "using Pkg; Pkg.instantiate()"
```

This downloads all Julia package dependencies listed in `Project.toml`.

## 6. Run the tests (optional)

```bash
pixi run julia --project -e "using Pkg; Pkg.test()"
```

All tests should pass. This also confirms that the test data is in place.

## 7. Train a model

The simplest model to start with is `LinearSurgeModel` — a single dense layer that predicts storm surge from wind stress and pressure. Training takes a few seconds.

```bash
bin/train examples/LinearSurgeModel.toml
```

Output (weights, loss plot, statistics) is written to `examples/training_output/example_LinearSurgeModel/`.

::: {.callout-note}
The example config uses `nepochs = 5` for a fast smoke-test. For a meaningful run increase this to 100 or more in the TOML file.
:::

## 8. Run inference

```bash
bin/predict examples/predict_LinearSurgeModel.toml
```

This loads the trained weights and runs prediction on the test period. Output is written to `examples/predict_output/example_predict_LinearSurgeModel/`.

## Next steps

- Explore the other example configs in `examples/` (ConvSurgeModel, ProductTideModel, …)
- Read the [settings reference](settings.md) to understand all available options
- Read the [data input settings](data_input_settings.md) to connect your own data
